newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's Zeroual urges cabinet to speed up reform.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's Zeroual urges cabinet to speed up reform.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual, chairing the first cabinet meeting of the new coalition government, on Monday urged ministers to speed up economic reforms and launch a huge job-creation programme.

Zeroual acknowledged that the task of government, in which seven Moslem fundamentalists are members, would not be easy. It had to strengthen stability in Algeria, where the government has been battling a Moslem militant insurgency for nearly six years.
It also had to boost the fledgling multi-party democracy in the nation of 29 million people and tackle the problem of the jobless and a chronic housing shortage.
More than two million people, mainly under the age of 30, are jobless, out of a workforce of about six million. The country also lacks an estimated two million housing units.

"You are entrusted with a difficult task in respect of the numerous transformations the country is undergoing but your mission is also exalting in respect to its noble objectives," Zeroual told the 38 cabinet members gathered at the presidential palace in Algiers.

The government, formed last week from the three main parties in the newly elected National Assembly (lower house), has yet to draw up a programme. This will have to be presented later to the house for a confidence vote.
Zeroual listed as priorities the maintenance of a state of law, the fight against corruption and red tap, and instilling a new momentum into reform of the economy.

Zeroual's supporters, who won the biggest share in the June general election under the flag of the National Democratic Rally (RND), control the main posts in the cabinet headed by Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia, one of Zeroual's staunchest backers.

Seven ministers and secretaries of state from the Islamist- oriented Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS) are in govenment alongside the same number of ministers and junior cabinet members from the former ruling Liberation National Front (FLN).
The RND gained 156 seats while the MPS and the FLN won 69 and 62 respectively in the June 5 legislative election.

"The first of my directives to the government is related to consolidating the state of law in our country. This state of law is not a slogan but a reality to which I adhere with conviction," said Zeroual, urging the cabient to strengthen the independence of the judiciary.

Zeroual ordered the government to carry out a dual economic strategy to give full speed to the reform programme by stepping up privatisation and restructuring the ailing state industrial sector and creating more jobs.

"The economic reforms already started should be pursed dynamically as regards industrial restructuring, financial system reform and the promotion of privatisation," he said in a presidential statement carried by the official Algerian news agency APS.
Zeroual also told Ouyahia to set up and head a taskforce to prepare the local elections expected to be held in October.
